Now that you have powder, you'll need to make it into clay before it's usable in any kind of structural piece.
To do that, you'll need to make powder blocks. Once you have a powder block of choice, you can place it in water like $(item)Concrete Powder$(), then break it to get clay balls!

$(item)Granite clay balls$() & $(item)Diorite clay balls$() can be crafted back into clay blocks too. Unlike the clay powder blocks, these don't fall and are unchanged by water, making them safe building blocks!
$(item)Granite clay balls$() & $(item)Diorite clay balls$() can be smelted into their respective bricks.
You can also smelt them into their respective brick blocks by smelting the clay blocks whole!

There are other important clays that aren't for structural use, but rather used to better control the temperature of a blade during $(thing)quenching$(). These kinds of clays are called $(term)Body$() and $(term)Slip$(). The use of $(term)Body$() and $(term)Slip$() during quenching helps the blade achieve two different levels of hardness. Without this method, a compromise of hardness to durability must be made, resultig in a lower quality blade overall.
